text:
Can you write an email to people who didn't renew their farm share? I run a 30-acre vegetable farm and sell 22-week shares that people pick up every Thursday.

Facts:
- Last year 260 households had a share. 97 didn't renew.
- On July 9 a hailstorm destroyed about half our crops. For the next 6 weeks the boxes had about half the usual amount. We didn't offer refunds or credit, and I sent one short email about it.
- A full share is $540 this year, the same as last year.
- This year we've added a second field on higher ground and put up 2 hail nets over our tomatoes and peppers. That cost $31,000.
- Members can now pause up to 2 weeks and get credit for them.
- Sign-up closes March 15. 52 shares are left.

Under 200 words.

Before I write this, a few questions. The people getting this email are upset about how the hail season was handled, so a few details will decide whether it lands:

1. **Is there anything for returning members specifically?** That could be a discount, a credit for last year's short weeks, or a bonus. They didn't get a refund or credit last year, and that's the main thing they'll hold against you. If there's nothing, I'll own it plainly instead of implying a make-good.
2. **Are you willing to say outright that you should have handled it differently?** For example, by communicating more or offering something at the time. An honest apology probably matters more to these readers than the $31,000.
3. **What does the second field protect against?** Higher ground sounds like flooding or drainage, not hail. I don't want to suggest it would have prevented last July's losses if it wouldn't have.
4. **What do the hail nets cover?** Only tomatoes and peppers, or other crops too? This decides how far I can promise "this won't happen again."
5. **Who signs it, and how do people sign up?** I need your name or the farm name, and the link or how to reply.
6. **Do you know why they didn't renew?** If anyone told you it was something other than the hail, like price, pickup day or moving away, I'll aim the email differently.

1. No discount or credit for last year. But this year I'll give a credit for any week weather cuts a box by more than a third.
2. Yes. I want to say sorry plainly. I only sent one email because I was working 16-hour days to save what was left, but I should have done better. This season I'll send a short email to members every Thursday.
3. I don't know.
4. Only the tomatoes and peppers, not the greens. I can't promise there won't be crop loss this year.
5. Sam Turner, Greenbank Farm. Sign-up is through the link on our website.
6. 41 of the 97 answered a short survey in the fall. 29 of them said they'd come back if we fixed how we handle bad weeks.

I've kept it under 200 words. Every fact you gave me is in the email except one: I didn't explain what the second field protects against, since you weren't sure. It's listed as part of what the $31,000 went to, with no claim that it would have prevented last summer's losses. I also didn't quote the survey numbers. "Many of you" is accurate for 29 of 41 replies, but saying 29 out of only 41 would remind readers that most people didn't answer.

<final_document>
Subject: We got last summer wrong. Here's what's changed.

Hi,

When hail destroyed about half our crops on July 9, your boxes ran half-full for six weeks. We offered no refund or credit, and I sent one short email. I was working 16-hour days to save what was left, but you deserved better. I'm sorry.

In our fall survey, many of you said you'd come back if we fixed how we handle bad weeks. So:

- If weather cuts a box by more than a third, you get credit for that week.
- I'll email members every Thursday, in good weeks and bad.
- You can pause up to two weeks and get credit for them.
- We've spent $31,000 on a second field on higher ground and hail nets over our tomatoes and peppers.

The nets don't cover the greens, and I can't promise there won't be crop losses. But if it happens, you'll hear about it from me, and you'll get credit.

A full share is still $540. Sign-up closes March 15, and 52 shares are left. The link is on our website.

I'd love to have you back.

Sam Turner
Greenbank Farm
</final_document>
